label: prf:content-genfun-palindromic
title: Proof that $C_n(q)$ is palindromic and bar-even via the conjugation anti-involution
html:
Proof. Proof that C_n(q) is palindromic and bar-even via the conjugation anti-involution

Proof.

Partition conjugation \lambda \mapsto \lambda' is an involution of the set of partitions of n. It is weight-preserving, f^{\lambda'} = f^\lambda (the standard tableaux of \lambda' are the transposes of those of \lambda), and content-reversing, \mathrm{content}(\lambda') = -\mathrm{content}(\lambda) (transposition exchanges the row and column indices, negating each cell's content j-i).

Palindromy. Reindexing the sum by conjugation,

C_n(q^{-1}) = \sum_{\lambda} f^\lambda q^{-\mathrm{content}(\lambda)}
= \sum_{\lambda} f^{\lambda'} q^{-\mathrm{content}(\lambda')}
= \sum_{\lambda} f^{\lambda} q^{\,\mathrm{content}(\lambda)} = C_n(q),

using f^{\lambda'}=f^\lambda and -\mathrm{content}(\lambda') = \mathrm{content}(\lambda).

Bar-even second order. Writing q = e^t, the linear term of C_n(e^t) in t is \sum_\lambda f^\lambda\,\mathrm{content}(\lambda); the same reindexing gives \sum_\lambda f^\lambda\,\mathrm{content}(\lambda) = \sum_\lambda f^{\lambda'}\,\mathrm{content}(\lambda') = -\sum_\lambda f^\lambda\,\mathrm{content}(\lambda), hence it is 0. So C_n(q) - C_n(1) has no linear term and is O((q-1)^2). Finally C_n(1) = \sum_\lambda f^\lambda = I(n) is the classical identity counting involutions by RSK shape. \blacksquare

Machine verification. The two structural steps — reindexing by an anti-invariant involution for palindromy, and the vanishing first moment for bar-evenness — are proved for arbitrary finite index sets in QOU.AntiInvolutionPalindrome (palindromic_sum_of_antiInvolution, first_moment_zero_of_antiInvolution), sorry-free. The Lean sibling checks the n=4 instance concretely (C4_palindromic, C4_first_moment_zero). Exact symbolic verification of the closed form, palindromy, C_n(1)=I(n) and the second-order rigidity for n \leq 8 is recorded in computations/lever1-content-monomial-separation.witness.json; the parallel result for the Plancherel weight (f^\lambda)^2 is in computations/lever1-plancherel-content-separation.witness.json.
